Done. Here's what changed in `init.md`:

### Skills added (4 loaded)
| Skill | Why |
|---|---|
| `context-engineering` | AGENTS.md structure optimization (was already there) |
| `memory-system` | Persist init results for cross-session retrieval |
| `ubiquitous-language` | Extract and record domain terms from the codebase |
| `git-workflow-and-versioning` | Set branch naming, commit conventions |

### Phases added
| Phase | What it does | Source |
|---|---|---|
| **Before You Init** | Guardrails — don't overwrite, validate commands, keep minimal | Ousterhout (complexity-first) |
| **Phase 4: Set Git Conventions** | Branch naming, commit style, merge strategy | PragProg (care about craft) |
| **Phase 5: Establish Vocabulary** | Extract 5-10 domain terms from types/modules, record as glossary | Evans DDD + Pocock (reduces "AI does wrong thing") |
| **Phase 7: Detect Broken Windows** | Flag outdated configs, dead CI, mixed conventions | PragProg (broken windows theory) |
| **Phase 9: Persist to Memory** | Store init results as observation for future sessions | Memory-system |
| **Phase 10: Verify and Report** | 9-point checklist + output report | — |

### Principles embedded
- **Minimal AGENTS.md** (<60 lines) — every line is a constraint on future agents
- **Command validation** — each detected command must actually work (not assumed)
- **Glossary from day 1** — prevents ambiguity before it starts
- **Broken windows flagged** — catch decay early before it normalizes

Here's the analysis:

### `ui-review` (general)
- Reviews ANY UI: components, pages, screenshots
- Scores 6 categories: typography, color, layout, interactivity, accessibility, polish
- Flags `--responsive`, `--dark-mode` modes

### `ui-slop-check` (specialized)
- Scans for AI-specific slop patterns: gradient abuse, shadow overuse, wrong spacing hierarchy
- Targets diffs/changed files via `--staged`, `--since=<ref>`
- Outputs a slop score (0-10)
- Built on the same 3 skills + same vision model

### The overlap

| Aspect | ui-review | ui-slop-check |
|---|---|---|
| Skills loaded | mockup-to-code + accessibility-audit + frontend-design | same 3 |
| Agent type | vision | vision |
| Model | proxypal/gemini-3-pro-preview | same |
| Output format | severity-grouped findings | slop score + findings |
| Input | image/component path | path, staged files, commit range |

### Verdict

**Yes, combine — but keep them as flags, not a merge.**

`ui-slop-check` is a **stricter, more targeted subset** of `ui-review`. The slop patterns (shadows, gradients, spacing) are exactly the things a general UI review would flag under "Visual Polish" — just with a slop-specific score and diff-targeting.

Merge as:
```
/ui-review <path>            → general UI review (current behavior)
/ui-review --slop <path>     → anti-slop audit with score
/ui-review --staged          → review staged changes for UI issues
```

This cleans up 30→**19 prompts** and removes the confusion of "which UI command do I use?"
